why.title: The world is running out of compute.
why.act1Body: AI training compute has doubled roughly __every six months__^4^ since 2010. NVIDIA posted [[$89 billion]]^1^ of data-center revenue in a single quarter — and its CEO says demand still runs far ahead of what the company can supply.
why.act1Cap: NVIDIA data-center revenue, year over year (Q2 FY2027)
why.act2Body: The bottleneck is no longer just chips. U.S. data-center vacancy sits at a record-low [[1.4%]]^2^, and chips wait in inventory with no power to plug them into^3^. Centralized compute is hitting __land, grid and cooling__.
why.act2Cap: Of capacity under construction already pre-leased (CBRE, H1 2026)
why.act3Body: Not every AI job needs a flagship GPU — image, language and speech inference run on hardware people already own. Volunteers’ idle devices once outran the world’s __top 500 supercomputers combined__^6^. Today there are [[8.8 billion]]^5^ mobile connections on Earth. NexGrid puts that pool to work.
why.quote1: “NVIDIA compute is fully utilized across every cloud we serve.”
why.quote2: “You may actually have a bunch of chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in.”

nex.faq3Q: What determines the price of NEX?
nex.faq3A: Supply and demand: inference-driven minting, buybacks, and the burn mechanism shape supply; platform usage shapes demand. Prices can go down as well as up.
nex.faq4Q: How is NEX different from a memecoin?
nex.faq4A: NEX is minted only when real AI work completes and has defined in-platform utility — it is not a speculative meme asset.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: A distributed AI compute network. Idle phones and dedicated devices run AI tasks, and their owners get paid for the work completed.
faq.a2: Install the app, connect your phone's idle compute, and tasks run automatically. You can scale up later with dedicated devices. Real-time earnings show inside the app.
faq.q3: Do I have to spend money to start?
faq.a3: No. The phone tier is free — no hardware, no deposit. Paid devices are optional and add compute capacity.
faq.q4: How do I know the earnings are real?
faq.a4: Every completed task generates a Proof-of-Compute receipt recorded on the platform ledger with on-chain attestation. Your app shows the full receipt trail for every payout.
faq.a5: Dedicated devices run in professional datacenters — no shipping, no home setup. Your device activates shortly after purchase and appears in your app.
faq.a6: Earnings settle in USDT inside the app, and you withdraw USDT to your own wallet. The app walks you through it step by step.
faq.q7: Will it drain my battery or overheat my phone?
faq.a7: It's managed — work is scheduled to respect battery and heat, so plugged-in, cool devices do more. You can turn phone compute off anytime in the app.
faq.q8: Which countries is NexGrid available in?
faq.a8: The sign-up flow in the app decides availability — it is the authoritative check for your region.
faq.a9: Starting is free. USDT withdrawals carry a network confirmation fee, shown on the withdrawal screen before you confirm; you can burn NEX to offset it.
faq.q10: Why would AI companies pay for compute on everyday devices?
faq.a10: Not every AI job needs a flagship data-center GPU. Image, language and speech inference run well on consumer hardware — and top-tier compute is booked out (NVIDIA says its compute is fully utilized across every cloud it serves), so demand spills into every layer. Distributed networks of everyday devices have reached supercomputer scale before: Folding@home hit 2.4 exaFLOPS in 2020, more than the top 500 supercomputers combined at the time.
